CHAPTER 1 / BEGINNINGS

Introduction

This book is an attempt to develop an interconnected account of algebra, beginning with the language of sets, maps, and the properties that characterize constructions.

Rather than presenting groups, rings, and fields as isolated collections of definitions and results, the project asks what constructions persist between these settings, how they arise, and how universal properties clarify their relationships.
